https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/09/labour-wins-holborn-st-pancras-byelection-green-party

Guardian: Labour fends off Green party to win Holborn and St Pancras byelection. By Sammy Gecsoyler and Peter Walker. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-09T08:14:43Z (09:14 BST); dateModified 09:52Z (10:52 BST); page states 'First published on Fri 9 Oct 2026 03.03 BST'.
Abdi-Wali 12,292 (45%) to Polanski 8,928 (33%). Turnout 38.7% - 'the lowest for any byelection held in England during this parliament and 15.4 percentage points down from the 2024 general election'.
KEY ARITHMETIC: 'the 8,928 votes cast for Polanski compared to the nearly 11,350 his party and the independent, pro-Gaza candidate Andrew Feinstein received combined in the seat in 2024 suggests the Greens have not significantly expanded their base of voters in the constituency'.
Abdi-Wali, former child refugee from Somalia (arrived 1990s), hit out at 'those who seek to divide us' - apparent response to Reform UK's Zia Yusuf, who suggested she was not British shortly after the byelection was called.
Bridget Phillipson (Labour chair) to Times Radio: 'It demonstrates that Labour's message of hope is really cutting through, that people don't just want parties like Labour to talk about the progressive change this country needs, but they want to see it delivered in action.'
Polanski: 'Of course I can carry on as leader of the Green party. We're a party of 220,000 members. I've taken a loss tonight but our movement is so much bigger than one election or one motion and we're going to grow.'
Polanski: 'we are going to be more of an electoral threat to Labour than we ever have in our history'.
Polanski on the motion: 'I would have supported the motion as amended. It wasn't amended, so no.'
Polanski on missing the vote: campaigners 'wanted to see me on the ground... They wanted to see me dealing with local issues. So I did exactly that.'
Abdi-Wali to the Guardian: people at the school gates found the Greens motion 'divisive', adding 'It just speaks to the larger divisive discourse that set off and I don't want to engage in that kind of thing.' On Labour and Palestine: 'The work Ed Miliband has been doing on Gaza, Palestine and Israel has resonated really well with local people. He's been taking action and not just speaking.'
Motion passed despite opposition from four of its five MPs. Greens took control of three London councils in May. Greens won Gorton and Denton byelection in February.
Low turnout suggests Burnham still faces an uphill battle in urban areas.
